lignes.texte: The internet is collapsing. Scroll through your feed and
you’ll notice it. Every piece of content you consume is turning into mindless lines of code.
No artist. No writer sitting at a desk. No editor tweaking a frame. No voice over artist reading
off a script. And no soul. We’re being drowned in an
endless flood of low-quality AI slop. And the worst part isn't that the technology
exists. It’s that the platforms hosting it refuse to tell you what is real and what is automated.
Creators are being suffocated by server farms, and everyday people are being robbed by algorithms.
The digital world as we know it, is under attack… And it’s time to do something about it.
The rapid rise of AI has changed the way we view the world. And it’s taken over. What started as
an experimental tool has transformed into a way to maximize efficiency and cut costs. Companies
are actively replacing employees with AI, using it for customer service agents and even flooding
search engines with artificial data. And it’s not just the corporations.
More and more people are using it across the internet. They use it for social media,
to build websites and mass produce content. And as the technology advanced,
the darker side started to emerge. Back in its infancy AI content was a
joke. The 6 fingered humans with robotic voices joke made it easy even for a non-tech-savvy
person to distinguish AI generation from real content. But things have changed since then.
Today, AI-generated content is becoming far more difficult to discern from the
real thing. The latest generative models can mimic human voices with 99.99% accuracy in
the fraction of a second. They can create hyper-realistic images and near-flawless
“deepfake” videos with incredible effectiveness. But the real casualty of this AI goldrush?
Creativity. AI slop is single-handedly leading
the charge towards the total devaluation of human effort, creativity, and skill.
Human creators put time and effort into their work. All the videos,
the writing and art is a process. It demands passion and patience, too. Even something as
seemingly simple as a video about video games or a pencil sketch of an original character
takes a lot out of the person that made it. They can spend days, weeks, and even months
crafting it. They need to edit, adjust, and refine, before sharing what they made with the
world. It might not be perfect… But it’s human.
The end product of genuine effort. A genuine expression of real creativity.
Then there’s AI AI bots and server farms can
churn out literally hundreds of pieces of content in a matter of minutes. Images, blog posts, and
videos all thrown out into the digital ether with a single click of a button. They’re not thought
about, drafted, and refined… they’re generated. And the people behind that kind of content don’t
care about quality. They only care about quantity. They know that if they saturate your feed with
enough slop, some of it will have an impact. Some of it will be seen,
some of it will be engaged with, and some of it will give them money, attention, and influence.
Real human creators, meanwhile, are completely lost in the crowd. Their
creations utterly submerged in the swamps of slop. They’re fighting a losing battle with algorithms.
Even the most passionate and talented creators can’t keep up with machines that produce 500
times as much content as they can. Not when social media algorithms are designed to
reward volume and frequency above all else. The team at the Infographics Show aren’t
anti-technology. Of course we’re not. And we’re not anti-AI, either.
Like we’ve said before, we use it as a tool, not a replacement. We use it to change text on
a thumbnail, without a producer needing photoshop experience. We use it to autogenerate sheets so
our directors can break down a script. We use it to upscale a video from normal HD to 4K so
it’s more TV friendly. But that’s it.
We have a highly talented human team who work hard to research, write and animate every single video.
And of course, bring it to life through voiceover. Seriously, I’m human… I see the comments.
So, we're not against AI as a concept. It’s a powerful piece of technology
that has the potential to do a lot of good in this world… as long as it’s
used responsibly and by the right people. Our problem isn’t the fact that AI exists.
Our problem is about how it’s being used. Especially the failure of major platforms to
be honest and transparent about it. They’re not powerless.
They already have the technology they need to detect and label AI-generated content.
They know when files were made by automated bots and AI server farms. And they have more
than enough money, resources, and influence to implement and enforce strict classification
systems that differentiate between human-made and AI-generated content.
But they don’t do it. Because, for them,
it’s not about right and wrong. It’s not about responsibility and ethics.
It’s about profit. Pure and simple.
It doesn’t matter whether a video was made by a human or a machine. If it gets views, clicks,
and engagement, then that means it also creates more ad revenue for the platform that hosts it.
These companies are deliberately treating human passion, deepfake scams,
and server-farm spam as the exact same thing. As long as it keeps you scrolling,
it’s all the same in their eyes. They’re actively profiting off the death of creativity,
and as long as the CEOs and shareholders are lining their pockets, they’re not going to change.
They've proven time and time again that their number one priority is engagement. Everything else
– be it user safety, ethics, or even the survival of human creativity – is far less important.
They’ve made their position clear. So we’re doing the same.
We’re joining Team Human, a new campaign built by creators to keep humans in control of AI.
This isn’t some sort of corporate partnership or sponsored ad deal.
It’s a movement, involving some of the biggest creators and channels on the internet,
with a combined reach of over 350 million followers and subscribers. We’re standing up
and making a statement about how we feel. And, in case it wasn’t already clear,
we’re frustrated and worried about the way the internet is heading. And the world broadly.
As we speak, tech giants and global governments are locked in a high-stakes arms race to deploy
increasingly intelligent AI models ahead of their rivals. They are completely blind
to the societal collapse occurring all around them. A collapse that’s a direct
result of their actions. That’s the bad news.
The good news is that the world is edging closer towards real, enforceable and
impactful international regulations. Major powers are starting to show a
willingness to take control of the situation and set up stricter guardrails. They want
to slow down the reckless development of dangerous and barely-vetted technologies.
Numerous AI safety experts have urged for these kinds of regulations to be put in place and
argued that guardrails are necessary in order to protect humanity from a potential catastrophe.
But it’s up to the public to actually show policymakers that this is what they want, too.
And we can make that happen. Our goal is simple, but vital
for the future of humanity. We want 200,000 people to sign the official
pledge at teamhuman.org before November 1st. The Center for AI Safety says this should be
enough to help public interest groups and AI safety advocates exactly what they need:
enough leverage to drag world leaders to the table and force them to pass long-overdue legislation.
If you want to keep humans in control of AI, stop deepfake scams, and make sure that real
human art doesn’t become a relic of the past, head to teamhuman.org and add your name to the pledge.
The more people sign, the louder our collective voices become. That’s how we show politicians we
don’t just want change, we demand it. Because if we don’t act
soon… it might be too late. We’re already approaching a dangerous tipping
point. The pivotal moment that the internet and the world, as we know it, changes forever.
The pace of AI development is rapidly outpacing our own ability to keep it
under control. If we let it continue without proper safety standards and platform labeling,
we risk losing control of the internet forever. And if we don’t hit the emergency brake right now,
the internet will become little more than a digital dump, bursting at the
seams with AI-generated garbage. We don’t want to see that.
There’s space for AI-generated content on the internet.
But there also needs to be space for what made it great to begin with… people.
The team at The Infographics Show has already signed up. You should too. Click the link in
the description and let’s show the politicians and platforms that we demand a slowdown.
